subject.title: Per-agent tools.selfDeny — allow tool inheritance to subagents while denying direct use

question: Should OpenClaw add a per-agent delegate-only/self-deny tool policy, and should it be modeled as `tools.selfDeny`, `delegateOnly`, scoped allow entries, or a follow-up to per-spawn `toolsAllow`?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the change adds public config surface and changes a security boundary for how requester tool policy flows to subagents.

options.title: Approve delegate-only config
options.body: Add an optional per-agent policy that hides tools from the requester model while preserving explicit deny-wins behavior and controlled child inheritance.

options.title: Fold into per-spawn policy
options.body: Let the `toolsAllow` work own child narrowing and document that parent direct-use prevention remains separate until a later design.

options.title: Keep monotonic policy only
options.body: Reject delegate-only inheritance and document the separate-agent or profile workaround as the intended security model.

recommendation.title: Approve delegate-only config
recommendation.body: Add an optional per-agent policy that hides tools from the requester model while preserving explicit deny-wins behavior and controlled child inheritance.

likelyOwner.reason: Vincent is the strongest current-main routing signal from recent merges and adjacent tool-policy ownership in the inspected history.
